title: Activation week slate and risk anchors — midyear planning draft
summary: Working sketch for the midyear activation week: an all-hands + exec update package, proposed cascading OKR language, cross-functional asks, and a short contingency register for high-risk items. Designed to be compact (25–30 minute all-hands) + 45m deep-dive breakout options for eng and product leaders.
body:
Purpose:
- Build a narrow, memorable narrative for activation week that ties product wins (runtime improvements, Dedicated capacity rollout, private deployment pilot) to the company mission (production-grade inference economics).
- Surface the minimal set of executive asks for each org so teams can finalize pre-reads.
- Capture top-line risks and one-line fallbacks so the CEO and CTO have crisp responses during Q&A.

Audience:
- All employees (AT the all-hands); Execs and Directors (prep for tabletop and breakout sessions); Sales/CS (short exec talking points).

High-level framing (2 minutes):
- Where we started (latency/cost problem for customers).
- What we shipped in the last 6 months: Dedicated GA improvements (stable autoscaling policy), streaming + tools integration in Redwood API, pilot private VPC for two enterprise customers.
- Why the next 90 days matter: convert momentum into sustainable commits (reserved capacity signups, private wins, and productized Optimize insights).

All-hands proposed slate (25–30m):
1) Fireside (7m): CEO high-level narrative + one customer highlight (short video clip, 60s).
2) Product demo (8m): Head of Product shows two flows: (a) Hosted API latency now vs baseline (demo + short dashboard), (b) Rollouts: canary -> A/B -> fallback chaining in Console.
3) Engineering (6m): Key runtime perf wins and an explicit story about unit-economics reduction (% tokens saved with KV caching + quantization guidance).
4) Ops & GTM ask (4m): concrete calls-to-action (sales: target 8 reserved capacity pilots; SRE: weekend readiness checklist).
5) Live Q&A (5m) + parking-lot followups.

Optional breakout sessions (45m each; sign-up):
- Eng deep dive: inference kernel selection and sequence length tuning (for serving-runtime and infra).
- Product & CS: framework for customer success playbooks for private deployments.
- GTM: scaled field motion for reserved capacity (pricing experiments).

Proposed company-level OKRs (draft language; minimal and measurable):
Objective A: Make inference predictable and cheaper for production customers.
- KR A1: Reduce median per-token cost on hosted API by 18% (benchmarked across 3 representative workloads).
- KR A2: Achieve 95th percentile P95 latency <= target (model-class specific; baseline + X ms) for top-3 hosted model families.
- KR A3: Sign 6 Dedicated reserved capacity contracts (monthly or annual) representing $Y ARR (placeholder).

Objective B: Expand private deployment adoption for regulated customers.
- KR B1: Ship private control plane GA with KMS integrations and audit logs (two vetted cloud partners).
- KR B2: Complete 2 on-prem pilot deployments and capture 4 customer success stories / testimonials.

Objective C: Reduce operational cost variability and failure blast radius.
- KR C1: Implement automatic fallback routing policy and validate through 3 chaos exercises.
- KR C2: Reduce incident MTTR by 30% vs last quarter via tracing + runbook improvements.

Cross-functional asks to include in pre-reads (one-liners):
- Product: finalize one low-friction Optimize recommendation that can be surfaced in Console (owner: Sofia).
- Eng-serving-runtime: freeze the next kernel opt change and bake regression tests for perf (owner: Marco).
- SRE: finalize weekend readiness and escalation tree for Dedicated launches (owner: Ethan).
- Sales/CS: commit to a list of 12 prioritized reserved capacity targets and a one-pager for pilots (owner: Head of Sales).

Risk anchors (top 6, short contingency for execs):
1) Performance regression from kernel change before activation week -> Contingency: rollback flag + hold canary windows; exec ask: approve emergency patch window.
2) Delayed legal review for private pilot contracts -> Contingency: ship with narrow scope + new template; exec ask: approve temporary exception.
3) One large prospective Dedicated customer delays go/no-go -> Contingency: ramp smaller pilots to replace expected revenue; exec ask: prioritize pricing flexibility.
4) Console demo flakiness during live all-hands -> Contingency: pre-recorded clip and live smoke-check; exec ask: allow fallback to recording.
5) Key engineering resource pull (people pulled to critical incident) -> Contingency: pre-assign secondary owners; exec ask: agree pause for non-critical changes.
6) Negative partner press or bug in production -> Contingency: rapid customer directive + joint postmortem; exec ask: sign-off on external comms template.

Exec update talking points (short bullets; for CEO/CTO):
- Customer momentum: pilot wins in finance and health verticals; highlight one measurable reduction in token cost from an early adopter.
- Product velocity: shipped X features that materially affect unit economics (batching, KV caching, routing).
- Risks and mitigation: top 3 risks summarized and ask of leadership (time-limited approvals).
- Metrics to watch for next 30 days: reserved capacity trial conversion rate, P95 latency trends, incident MTTR.

Pre-reads (attachable one-pagers):
- One-pager: "Why Reserved Capacity matters" (GTM + finance checks).
- Tech note: "Regression testing plan for kernel rollout" (serving-runtime).
- Sales checklist: pilot onboarding steps for private deployments.

Logistics & owner matrix (one-liners):
- All-hands logistics: AV booked, pre-recorded clip set (owner: People Ops).
- Slides & deck: 10-slide max; get exec review two days before (owner: Priya).
- Breakout signups: use internal form + cap at 60 per session (owner: Org Ops).

Notes to self / unresolved questions:
- Decide whether to push KR thresholds up after current benchmark runs finish (still waiting on QPS matrix from perf team).
- Need a short script for the CEO Q&A with suggested responses to the 6 risks above.
- Confirm that marketing has a one-page for the marketplace listing for Dedicated.

Appendix (evidence snippets we can paste into the deck):
- Before/After perf snapshot: median per-token CPU+GPU cost for three sample prompts (raw numbers placeholder).
- Customer quote rough draft: 'Redwood made our inference predictable and reduced our per-request jitter' (to be validated).
- Short demo checklist for streams + fallback path.

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Finalize OKR language with execs (Owners: Priya + CTO) by EOD Wed.
- Product to produce one concrete Console screenshot for the all-hands demo (Sofia, due Thu).
- Eng to lock the kernel change freeze and produce regression perf run (Marco, due Fri).
- Ops to circulate pre-read and the breakout signup form (Org Ops, due Thu).

Tone/Style guidance for the deck:
- Tight, outcome-oriented, one-customer anecdote, one technical screenshot, one ask for leadership.
- Avoid long technical deep dives on the main stage; use breakouts for those.

End of draft.

(Owners: Priya Malhotra; please ping collaborators for edits. This is intentionally concise — will expand KRs to numeric placeholders once perf bench completes.)
